recent_posts.title: Real world refactoring of a scattered AI tool architecture using agentic coding
recent_posts.summary: A real-world walkthrough of refactoring a scattered AI tool-calling architecture in a TypeScript monorepo into a consolidated, maintainable AI package. The author starts with tool definitions spread across three packages, uses Claude and GPT-4.5 as agentic coding assistants to iteratively consolidate everything into a single AI package with compile-time safety. The process reveals the tension between 'derive everything from one registry' (which creates unreadable types) versus 'explicit mirrors with strict typing' (which is more verbose but understandable). Key lessons include: asking 'how many steps to add a new tool?' as an architecture smell test, preferring compile-time errors over runtime surprises, and knowing when to switch AI models — Claude for initial exploration, GPT-4.5 for strict TypeScript work. A re-entrancy bug introduced by awaiting a non-awaitable AI SDK callback is also debugged live.

recent_posts.title: Why I build differently than I teach and what I am changing
recent_posts.summary: A YouTube coding educator (Code with Antonio) reflects on the gap between how he builds software privately versus how he teaches it publicly. His current method involves pre-building projects, then re-recording them cleanly — resulting in tutorials where everything works first try but viewers only learn to copy steps, not think independently. He distinguishes between vibe coding (outcome-focused, minimal human input) and agentic coding (developer as architect, using AI to amplify skills with precise prompts). Using agentic coding, he can now compress hundreds of hours of real development into digestible sessions, enabling him to record himself building for the first time rather than re-recording. This led him to create a paid two-week workshop on codewithantonio.com where modules drop progressively, showing his actual thought process and technical decision-making rather than dictating lines of code.

Build Your Own Lovable Clone - Full Stack Agentic AI Website Builder with Inngest & Nextjs 15
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial for building an AI-powered website builder similar to Lovable using Next.js 15, React 19, tRPC, Prisma, and various modern tools. The tutorial covers setting up a full-stack application with database integration, authentication via Clerk, background jobs with Inngest, and secure code execution using E2B sandboxes. It includes proper Git workflow practices, AI code generation capabilities, and deployment strategies for creating a production-ready SaaS application.

recent_posts.title: Build and Deploy a Multi Vendor E Commerce With Nextjs, React & Stripe Connect (Part 2/2)
recent_posts.summary: This tutorial demonstrates building a multi-vendor e-commerce platform with Next.js, React, and Stripe Connect. Part 2 covers implementing the complete purchase flow including cart functionality using Zustand for state management, checkout pages, product reviews, vendor subdomains, and deployment. The tutorial addresses common issues like Node.js version compatibility and hydration errors when using client-side storage. Key features include tenant-specific carts, dynamic loading to prevent SSR mismatches, and a responsive product view with ratings and vendor information.

recent_posts.title: Build a YouTube Clone with Next.js 15: React, Tailwind, Drizzle, tRPC (Part 2/2)
recent_posts.summary: Part 2 of building a YouTube clone focuses on creating the video page with three main sections: video player, user information with subscription features, and reactions. The tutorial covers implementing tRPC procedures with SQL joins to fetch video data along with author information, creating reusable UI components for video display, user avatars, and interactive elements like like/dislike buttons and dropdown menus. Key features include video view tracking using a composite primary key schema, description expansion boxes, and responsive layout design. The implementation uses advanced database concepts like inner joins and subqueries to optimize data fetching, while maintaining proper component architecture with prefetching and caching strategies.

recent_posts.title: Build a Jira Clone With Nextjs, React, Tailwind, Hono.js | Part 2/2 (2024)
recent_posts.summary: This tutorial demonstrates building a comprehensive Jira clone application using Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, and Hono.js. It covers implementing project management features including creating projects within workspaces, building CRUD operations for projects, setting up database collections with proper permissions, creating API endpoints with authentication middleware, implementing file upload functionality for project avatars, building forms with validation using Zod schemas, and creating settings pages for project management. The tutorial also covers error handling, loading states, and proper routing structure for a multi-tenant workspace application.

recent_posts.title: Build a Real-Time Slack Clone With Nextjs, React, Tailwind, Auth.js | Part 2/2 (2024)
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial covering the implementation of a Slack clone's messaging system, including emoji selection, image upload functionality, database schema design for messages and conversations, and real-time chat features. The tutorial demonstrates building editor components with Quill.js, handling file uploads with Convex storage, creating database relationships for channels, messages, and reactions, and implementing proper state management for chat interfaces.
